# 5. Interaction Flow Based on the above functional architecture and the integration model of Agent/Copilot, this chapter focuses on how to achieve end-to-end processing of the Individual Mobile Service Delivery through the interaction and cooperation of agents at the Network operation layer and the Service operation layer. The functionalities in the business operations layer and corresponding interaction below are only used as examples to illustrate the end to end procedure. This document mainly focusses on the interactions between service operation layer and network operation layer. ## 5.1. AN L4 individual mobile service delivery Interaction Flow [Figure: Figure 3. AN L4 individual mobile service delivery Interaction Flow] For AN L4 individual mobile service delivery, the Radio Service Handling Agent operates in an autonomous closed-loop mode and interacts with the Individual Mobile Service Delivery Agent for cross RAN domains coordination, which includes following procedures: - **Step1:** represents the request for individual mobile service delivery intent (e.g. offering living streaming service packages at the xx Venue). The Individual Mobile Service Delivery Agent generate the radio service intent template based on the individual mobile service delivery intent. - **Step2:** represents the request for configuration of the radio service intent templates (including supported scene, supported service SLA targets, assurance time). The Radio Service Handling Agent maintain all radio service intent templates for different individual mobile service packages. - **Step3:** represents the request for radio service intent exploration to explore the service capacity (maximum number of UEs possible to subscribe and access the individual mobile service with expected SLAs) for specified regions and radio service intent template. Based on the request, the Radio Service Handling Agent performs the exploration process to evaluate and determine the best possible values for the service capacity (Maximum number of UEs) considering current resource situation and capabilities of the radio network. - **Step4:** represents the response to obtain the radio service intent exploration report, including the maximum number of UEs possible to subscribe and access the individual mobile service with expected SLAs. This step will be periodically triggered by the Radio Service Handling Agent based on the specified report period (e.g., 15 minutes, 1 hour). - **Step5:** represents the steps that business operation layer query the service capacity information which can be used for user subscription. - **Step6:** represents the steps that UE request to subscribe the individual mobile service package. - **Step7:** represents the steps that business operation layer request to check the feasibility of user’s the subscription for the individual mobile service. - **Step8:** represents the request for radio service intent feasibility check to confirm whether the radio service in the specified geo coordinate is feasible for subscription. Based on the request, the Radio Service Handling Agent performs the feasibility check activities to determine whether the radio service in the specified geo coordinate is feasible for subscription and access based on available radio network resource. - **Step9:** represents the response to obtain the radio service intent feasibility check report. - **Step10:** represents steps for the configuration user’s subscription information to enable the user successfully access the subscribed mobile service. ## 5.2.
